title: C340 — Inline connector reference
introduction:
There is more going on in driver-seat wiring than making the seat scoot. This inline reference includes seat power, grounds, sensors, network connections and restraint-related circuits. I read it like a seating chart: choose the correct face, find the labeled cavity, then consult its row. A familiar wire color is a clue, not an address.

Read Circuit Number together with Function, then use that face’s Color, Gauge and Terminal Part Number entries. Keep the network’s HIGH and LOW labels distinct, retain restraint polarity labels, and preserve the fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternatives in supply descriptions. Treat the different ground descriptions separately rather than assuming every ground row names the same connection. Repeated rows without qualifiers do not establish which configuration applies.

The drawings show cavity locations and housing features, without an explicit physical viewing direction or a shading legend. Gauge conventions, Size/Used codes and the blocked terminal entry are not decoded here. This is an identification guide, with unresolved assignments noted for review. It supplies no access, release, restraint-system preparation, probing or repair procedure; hands-on work requires the applicable service information.

edits.why: The lower-numbered cavity group is on the left in this illustration. Its end positions sit farther outward than the central rows, so I follow the labels rather than assuming a uniform grid. Gray positions appear in the other group near the top and bottom. The asymmetric housing projections help distinguish the view without establishing a release movement.

Use the function labels to separate seat power, battery logic, buckle and track sensing, network connections, grounds and restraint circuits. The HIGH and LOW network labels identify distinct connections; polarity marks likewise belong to their stated restraint functions. A shared housing does not make these circuits interchangeable, and the table gives no electrical pass/fail criteria.

The higher-numbered cavity group is on the left here, with the lower-numbered group on the right. The outward end positions and large right-side housing projection help identify this particular illustration. I use its cavity labels directly instead of mentally mirroring the male view. No projection is identified as a latch or release.

Read this face independently: supply and ground circuit names can differ from the male entries, and the restraint descriptions also differ at corresponding cavity labels. Preserve those descriptions without declaring a verified end-to-end restraint map. Repeated ground entries with differing colors remain unresolved alternatives, while @BLOCKED@ is retained literally rather than treated as a usable terminal part number.

Keep each kit’s service part, engineering shell, material, gauge and cavity fields together as a separate catalog entry. The two entries for the female shell have different gauge and service-part fields; sharing a shell number does not establish interchangeability or select a repair kit. These listings do not provide installation instructions.

The Product Id is a separate regional catalog listing. The table does not associate it with a particular kit row above or supply installation instructions; do not infer either association from its placement.

originalAuthorHold: The female table repeats cavity 8, circuit GD233, with both BK and BK-GY wire colors and no applicability qualifier. The applicable color remains unresolved.

Corresponding restraint cavity labels carry different assignments: male cavity 12 is CR106 for the front-driver outboard seat-mounted air bag, while female cavity 12 is CR105 for the front-driver-side seat-mounted air bag; male cavity 14 is CR105 for the seat-mounted air bag, while female cavity 14 is CR109 for the driver-side inflatable curtain. No supplied qualifier explains the relationship. Review is needed before presenting a verified through-connection or component assignment.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 74 primary units, four complete pages/two figures and six edits. Original first CLI author covered 61 units/four headings. Complete draft adds pigtail and European catalog headings, all table rows and raw text coverage. Original partial author retained separately; physical restraint assignments, ground-color alternatives and blocked terminal identity remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
